sources.title: Cytokine Inhibition in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Patients
sources.key_finding: n=50; primary CIS-fatigue; results published as PMID 28265678 (not posted as CT.gov results module).

synthesis: The only adequately reported anakinra RCT in CFS (Roerink/Annals 2017) found no fatigue benefit versus placebo and numerically fewer responders on anakinra. Secondary cytokine work likewise showed no treatment effect. Negative controlled trial → tier D (contested/insufficient), not early-positive C.
limitations: Single-center, women-only, 4-week exposure. IL-1 blockade may still be relevant in other phenotypes, but current CFS RCT evidence is null. Injection-site reactions expected with anakinra.
confidence_notes: Deep-dive 2026-09-19: TIER CHANGED C→D after primary Annals RCT review. Prior evidence-eval-bot C superseded.

synthesis: AXA1125 has a peer-reviewed Phase 2a pilot (eClinicalMedicine 2023): primary mitochondrial MRS endpoint failed, but Chalder fatigue improved vs placebo over 4 weeks. Signal is early and single-centre—tier C appropriate; not B (failed primary, small n, short exposure, sponsor-era program uncertainty).
limitations: Failed primary bioenergetic endpoint. Fatigue secondary/exploratory framing in a pilot. No multicentre confirmatory RCT. Formulation/sponsor continuity unclear for larger development.
confidence_notes: Prior C retained. Replaced off-target review PMIDs with primary NCT05152849 / PMID 37223439.

synthesis: NorCAPITAL is a clear negative therapeutic RCT: low-dose clonidine attenuated sympathetic/inflammatory markers but worsened or failed to improve activity—the primary clinical goal—and authors state it is not clinically useful in adolescent CFS. Tier D.
limitations: Adolescent sample; adult ME/CFS may differ. Hypotension/sedation risks of clonidine. Sympathetic 'overactivity' may be compensatory—blunting it can harm function.

synthesis: Norwegian open-label Phase 2 reported meaningful fatigue responses after IV cyclophosphamide in ME/CFS, supporting biological plausibility of immune-modulating approaches. limitations: Open-label; no placebo. Chemotherapy-grade risks (infection, infertility, secondary malignancy, cytopenias). Not for routine care. RituxME failure cautions against over-generalizing B-cell/immune hypotheses.

tier_change_why: NCT05472090 primary daily pain NRS −2.2 (TNX-102 SL) vs −2.0 (placebo)—essentially no primary separation; no inferential stats posted → insufficient/null primary → D.

sources.title: Phase 2 Study of TNX-102 SL in Patients With Multi-Site Pain Associated With PASC
sources.key_finding: n=63; primary pain NRS nearly identical vs placebo; fatigue secondary numerically better (−8.0 vs −3.2) without posted p-values.

synthesis: TNX-102 SL (sublingual cyclobenzaprine) Phase 2 for PASC multi-site pain shows no meaningful primary pain separation from placebo on CT.gov. Exploratory fatigue numbers are not a substitute for a positive primary. Tier D.
limitations: Small n=63; missing posted inferential tests. Fibromyalgia TNX-102 program is a different indication. Sedation/anticholinergic AEs.
confidence_notes: Deep-dive: TIER CHANGED C→D for null/near-null primary.

sources.title: Valganciclovir for CFS patients with elevated HHV-6/EBV titers
sources.key_finding: n=30; results via publications, not CT.gov module.

synthesis: Small subset RCT + open-label work suggest possible benefit of valganciclovir in HHV-6/EBV-seropositive CFS, but sample size and generalizability are limited. Tier C—not B.
limitations: n≈30; selected seropositive subset. Myelosuppression/renal monitoring required. Viral antibody titers imperfect enrichment. Not guideline-endorsed standard care.
confidence_notes: Prior C retained. Primary Montoya RCT replaces off-target herpes/antiviral reviews.
